sql.objective: Fetch employees hired between 2024-01-01 and 2024-12-31 (both dates included).
options: SELECT * FROM employees WHERE hire_date FROM '2024-01-01' TO '2024-12-31';
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE hire_date BETWEEN '2024-01-01' AND '2024-12-31';
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE hire_date IN ('2024-01-01', '2024-12-31');
SELECT * FROM employees WHERE hire_date RANGE '2024-01-01' - '2024-12-31';

sql.objective: Find customers who have never placed a single order.

SELECT name FROM customers WHERE orders = 0;

sql.objective: Find email addresses that appear more than once in the users table.
options: SELECT email FROM users WHERE COUNT(email) > 1;
SELECT email FROM users ORDER BY email HAVING DUPLICATES;
SELECT email FROM users GROUP BY email HAVING COUNT(*) > 1;

sql.objective: Show each employee's salary along with the average salary of the whole company in the same result.

SELECT name, salary, AVG(salary) FROM employees;
SELECT name, salary, (SELECT AVG(*) FROM employees) FROM employees;
SELECT name, salary + AVG(salary) FROM employees GROUP BY name;

fullstack.explanation: getElementById() takes a plain id with NO '#' prefix — '#signup' should be 'signup' (querySelector uses '#', getElementById doesn't).
Strict === never treats string '25' as equal to number 25 — the condition is always false. Convert first (Number(age)) or use loose comparison.
var is function-scoped, so all the closures capture the SAME i — funcs[0]() returns 3, not 0. Using let in the loop fixes it.

python.explanation: Missing colon at the end of the if statement — Python throws a SyntaxError.
IndexError — a 3-item list has valid indexes 0, 1, 2. numbers[3] is out of range.
map() returns a lazy map object, not a list — it can't be indexed. Wrap it: list(map(...)) first.
If the input isn't a number, 'value' never gets assigned — the except swallows the error and print() crashes with NameError.

react.explanation: Typo: setCunt is not defined — ReferenceError. Should be setCount.
While user data is still loading, user is undefined — user.name crashes. Guard it: {user?.name} or give a default.
config is a brand-new object every render, so React re-runs the effect after EVERY render → infinite fetch loop. Depend on config.filter or memoize config.

mern.explanation: There is no app.start() — Express listens with app.listen(3000).
Missing 'await' before user.save() — the response is sent before the document is actually saved, and save errors are silently lost.

django.explanation: render() needs the request first: render(request, 'home.html') — leaving it out raises a TypeError.
Post.objects.all is missing parentheses — it passes the method itself, not the queryset. Should be Post.objects.all().

cybersecurity.explanation: The password is saved in plain text — it must be hashed first (e.g. user.set_password(...) or make_password(...)).
MD5 is broken for password hashing — it's fast and brute-forceable. Use a slow, salted algorithm like bcrypt, argon2 or PBKDF2.

cpp.explanation: 'cout' is undeclared — the file is missing 'using namespace std;' (or use std::cout).
Use-after-delete — after 'delete p', p is a dangling pointer and reading *p is undefined behavior.
i <= 3 reads arr[3], one past the end of a 3-element array — undefined behavior. The condition must be i < 3.
